_comment: Send SPA ROUTES to index.html, and nothing else.
This used to be /(.*), which matched everything — including requests for JavaScript.
Vercel applies a rewrite only when no static file matches, so a request for a chunk that
no longer exists (a browser holding the previous build, asking for the previous
filenames) fell through to index.html and was answered with HTML, 200 OK.
The browser then refused it: 'Expected a JavaScript-or-Wasm module script but the server
responded with a MIME type of text/html'. Angular abandoned the navigation and the click
did nothing at all — no error on screen, no redirect, just a dead menu item.
The negative lookahead excludes any path whose last segment carries a file extension, so
a missing .js or .css now returns an honest 404 instead of a page pretending to be a
script. Route paths (/voting, /recordings) have no extension and still reach index.html.
index.html must NEVER be served from cache. It is the file that names every other file,
and each build gives those files new hashed names.
This is what made a plain refresh useless after a deploy: the browser reused its cached
index.html, which still pointed at the previous build's chunks, so it asked for the same
missing files and failed the same way. Only Ctrl+Shift+R — which bypasses the cache —
recovered it. Expecting users to know that is not a plan.
no-cache does not mean 'do not store'. It means 'revalidate before use', so the browser
still gets a cheap 304 when nothing has changed, and the current file the moment it has.
The opposite rule for everything the build hashes. outputHashing is set to 'all', so a
given filename's contents can never change — a new build produces a new name. Content
that cannot change is safe to cache permanently, and caching it permanently is what keeps
the uncached index.html above cheap.
Source maps are covered too. They are only fetched when devtools are open.
